comment: The package MANIFEST: the entry points the core worker imports to boot the
agent paradigm. This is the single package index the worker reads (the
legacy scene.json asset/driver index was retired in E6.9). The worker
fetches THIS file first: if it carries an
'agents' block, the generic loader (engine/agents/loadPackage.js) imports
the declared modules and wires them into the AgentRuntime. The engine names
no domain — it mounts whatever this file declares.
All paths are RELATIVE to the package baseUrl (catalog.json), so the package
can be republished from a CDN with a one-field catalog change. The worker
resolves each path against that base; nothing here is an absolute URL.
agents.environment        the world module: exports createEnvironment(opts)
-> { bounds, cellAt, tick, snapshot, capabilities }.
agents.environmentOptions  passed verbatim to createEnvironment. 'seed' fixes
the PRNG so the same package replays the same
emergence (seeded determinism, no replay system).
agents.capabilities        OPTIONAL and unused here: this package's domain
verbs live under environment/verbs/ and
createEnvironment returns them as `capabilities`,
which the engine auto-registers. The environment is
the enabler, so there is no separate entry point.
agents.roster              the initial cast: exports createRoster(env, opts)
-> [agentSpec, ...].
render                     the L2 bindings module (archetype -> engine
primitive, referenced BY NAME) the host relay reads
to paint agents.state. Pure content, no browser APIs.
THE ONE RULE: every module named here is dependency-free ESM that runs
identically in the core Web Worker and in plain Node. None may touch
window/document/canvas/WebGL/Cesium/Maps/fetch. See dev/README.md.
